The snow fell softly below the small, cozy cabin nestled in the mountains. Inside, a warm fire crackled in the stone fireplace, casting flickering shadows on the rustic walls. The air was thick with the scent of pine and wood smoke, and the quiet was broken only by the occasional gust outside that rattled the windows. There were no distractions—just the simple joys of a weekend away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.

In the morning, before the sun had fully risen, I brewed a pot of coffee and sat by the fire to write. The quiet was a welcome relief, and I found myself lost in the rhythm of the pen on the paper. Outside, the snow had deepened, covering the forest in a blanket of white. It was the perfect backdrop for a peaceful walk later that day.

After lunch, I ventured out with my skis. The snow was thick and powdery, making each step a joy. The trees stood like sentinels, their branches heavy with snow. I skied below them, feeling a deep connection to the natural world around me. The cold air bit at my cheeks, but it was invigorating.

When I returned to the cabin, I found a small fire already going. The logs had been split and stacked neatly by my wood stove, a thoughtful gesture from the previous occupant. I added some more to the fire and sat by it, reading a book. The warmth of the flames and the crackle below them were comforting.

As the day drew to a close, I prepared a simple dinner of soup and bread. The cabin was quiet, save for the occasional sigh of contentment as I sipped my soup. Outside, the snow had stopped, and the world lay still under a blanket of night.

# Learning to Swim as an Adult

Entering the pool for first time can be daunting some choose to avoid it altogether. Not me I faced my fears and dove into the experience headfirst. Lessons began with basic breathing techniques and floating facedown or faceup in calm waters. Slowly instructor guided me into more challenging moves like kicking and arm movements. Practice made progress I could hold my breath longer and stay afloat longer each lesson. Building confidence in the water allowed deeper exploration of strokes and turns. Now I can swim laps across the pool with ease More soon.
